name: 広島つけ麺 弁慶 (Hiroshima Tsukemen Benkei)

claims.text: Core dishes are wheat-based (wheat tsukemen/ramen noodles and a soy-sauce-based dip), so a shared kitchen makes gluten avoidance impractical.
Hiroshima tsukemen is dipped in a soy-sauce-and-chili sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat.
Dishes are built on pork char siu and meat/sesame-based tantanmen, so animal products are central and shared.

name: 広島つけ麺 ぶちうま (Hiroshima Tsukemen Buchiuma)

claims.text: A wheat-noodle tsukemen shop with soy-sauce-based dipping broth; gluten is central to the menu and there is no indication of gluten-free handling or separation.
The dipping sauce is soy-sauce based (standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat); the broth is a chicken-pork-bone, seafood and tomato blend.
Broth is animal-based (chicken-pork bone plus seafood) and the dish is topped with pork chashu; no vegan or vegetarian preparation is documented.

name: 廣島つけ麺本舗 ばくだん屋 本店 (Hiroshima Tsukemen Honpo Bakudanya Honten)

claims.text: The dish is wheat-noodle tsukemen prepared in a shared noodle kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The signature spicy dipping sauce is a Japanese-style (wadafu) sauce, which conventionally uses wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free version is mentioned.
The bowl is notably vegetable-forward (cabbage, cucumber, green onion) and the spice level can be set to zero, so the heat itself is fully adjustable.
The kitchen centers on wheat noodles, so flour and gluten are present throughout; no gluten-free handling is mentioned.
The tsukemen dipping broth uses soy sauce, which in Japan is typically brewed with wheat.
Dishes feature pork (charred pork / chashu) and the broth is meat/fish based, so vegan dishes are not separated or available.

name: 本家うずしお（うずしお） (Honke Uzushio (Uzushio))

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside wheat batter and noodles, so any non-wheat order would face heavy cross-contact; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki is finished with a wheat-and-soy-based okonomiyaki sauce, which contains gluten.
Pork, egg, oysters and the same griddle are used across dishes, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.
Wheat-based okonomiyaki batter and yakisoba noodles are cooked on a shared teppan griddle, so heavy gluten cross-contact is unavoidable.
Hiroshima okonomi sauce is brushed on the finished okonomiyaki and is made with wheat-based soy sauce.
Pork, egg and dashi-based ingredients are cooked together on the same griddle as all dishes.

name: インド料理 チュリヤカナック (Indo Ryori Churiya Kanak)

claims.text: ハラール・ベジタリアン・ビーガンに対応した食事を用意しており、客の食の要望に応じて調理を調整すると明記。来店前の電話相談が可能。
ハラール認証に対応し、豚肉不使用、料理・店内ともにアルコール不使用。
ベジタリアン・ビーガン対応メニューを用意し、油控えめ・野菜中心の調理を掲げている。
ムスリム向けに無料の礼拝スペースを提供している。

name: インド料理ラソイ 本通り店 (Indo Ryori Rasoi Hondori-ten)

claims.text: The kitchen states it flexibly accommodates vegetarian and vegan menu requests, indicating staff will adjust dishes on request.
Vegetable curries and flexible vegetarian/vegan accommodation are available, so plant-based diners have on-request options.
